I'm a first-year PhD student in Health Policy at Harvard University, on the
economics track.

I (plan to) study markets for health care and the regulations that shape them, 
particularly for health insurance but also for medical services.
I'm interested in how regulations and market incentives interact 
to affect cost and availability of health care, and thus
health and financial outcomes for individuals. 


Before starting at Harvard I spent two years as a research assistant at the
**Federal Reserve Board**, in the Flow of Funds section, working with Board
economists on a variety of projects.
 As an undergraduate, I worked at the **Hilltop Institute** on hospital price
transparency, working with publicly posted pricing data across 31 states. I hold a BA
in Economics and Political Science from UMBC.

## Research interests

::: {.interests}
- Real effects of health insurance financing choices: RBC requirements, capital-motivated reinsurance, organizational structure
- Determinants of hospital pricing: integration in provider and insurance markets, insurance contracts, market power
- Private participation in publicly funded insurance programs: ACA marketplaces, Medicaid managed care, Medicare Advantage
:::

See [Research](research.qmd) for more, or the [CV](cv.qmd) for the full record.
